exposure: Group B streptococcus (GBS) colonization in late gestation
cohort: The study included 120 pregnant women in their third trimester infected with Group B streptococcus and 120 healthy pregnant women in their third trimester as a control group.
finding: GBS colonization in late pregnancy is correlated with vaginal micro-environment disorders and significantly increases the incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including intrauterine infection, neonatal infection, fetal distress, pathological jaundice, and lower neonatal Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was compared between groups, but no specific findings related to mode of birth were reported in the abstract.
followup_time: Immediate post-birth for neonatal outcomes (e.g., Apgar score, neonatal infection, fetal distress, pathological jaundice).
cross-section timing: GBS status and vaginal micro-ecology were assessed in late pregnancy (third trimester), with pregnancy and neonatal outcomes measured at birth and immediately postpartum.
